articles.headline: Steelers and Mike McCarthy just exposed why they're so hard to beat
keyFacts: Pittsburgh Steelers defeated the New Orleans Saints 16-10 in France during Week 7.
Jeremy Bergman of NFL.com noted that Pittsburgh controls games and grinds out wins even when their offense struggles.
The Steelers used long drives to kill the clock, wear down the Saints defense, and keep the Saints offense off the field.
body: The NFL's Week 7 games are winding down, and as always, there were lots of surprises and a few expected results. For the Pittsburgh Steelers, head coach Mike Tomlin and the team pulled off a much-needed win in France over the New Orleans Saints, 16-10.

The Steelers are looking stronger, and after seeing Sunday's game, it's becoming obvious what makes this team so difficult to beat. Sure, they have a strong offense with MVP-winning quarterback Aaron Rodgers, but there's more to it than just a simple offensive boost.
The Steelers can win even when their offense isn't at its best

What makes this team hard to beat is that the Steelers can control a game and grind out wins even when their offense isn't playing its best. That's something Jeremy Bergman of the NFL's official website points out in a takeaways piece about Week 7 showdowns.

"On the afternoon, Pittsburgh had only seven drives and found the end zone just once, but its long drives (four of 11-plus plays) killed clock, wearing down New Orleans' defense and keeping the Saints' offense off the field," he notes in the piece.

He adds, "An historic first game in France was just another walk in the park for Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers' offense. Pittsburgh's balanced attack, paced by Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle (season-high 86 total yards) with a smattering of splash plays from Rodgers, ran through a Saints defense that bent to the Steelers' will, but rarely broke."
So, the Steelers are proving once again that they're a force this season. Certainly don't count them out for a deep run.

articles.headline: Shadab Khan and Haris Rauf pull off miracle with record 89-run partnership for last wicket as Pakistan stun England in Lahore
keyFacts: Shadab Khan and Haris Rauf achieved a record-breaking 89-run partnership for the last wicket to secure a victory for Pakistan against England in Lahore.
Shadab scored an unbeaten 113 runs to help chase down England's target of 241, after Pakistan had been reduced to 154 for 9.
The victory advanced Pakistan into the tri-series final.
body: The game looked set for England when Haris Rauf walked out to bat at number 11 with Pakistan at 154 for 9 in their chase of 242, still needing 88 runs to win.

It looked like it was all over, and England certainly thought so. But Shadab Khan, who came in at number eight, did the unthinkable, stitching together an unbeaten 89-run partnership for the last wicket with Rauf to take Pakistan home in Lahore on Sunday. in the fourth ODI of the tri-series, which also features Sri Lanka.

Shadab chipped away at the target, finding a boundary in almost every over while managing to keep the strike with himself most of the time. Rauf played his part too, defending when needed and ducking and weaving as England threw everything at him. He hung in there to finish unbeaten on seven, while Shadab dictated terms at the other end. Rauf eventually hit the winning runs and raced away with his arms raised.

The unbeaten 89-run stand between Shadab and Rauf is now the highest for the 10th wicket in a successful ODI chase. The previous record was an unbeaten 64-run partnership between Deryck Murray and Andy Roberts against Pakistan at the 1975 World Cup.
Shadab scored his maiden ODI century, making 113 off 96 balls in a match-winning effort that turned the game on its head as England let victory slip away.
The win took Pakistan into the tri-series final.
— PakistanCrnrj (@PakistanCrnrj)

England had made a strong start while defending their target, with their bowlers working together to prevent Pakistan from building partnerships. Pakistan lost their top three batters — Fakhar Zaman (10 off 18), Saim Ayub (6 off 12) and Babar Azam (10 off 12) — inside the powerplay. England continued to take wickets and reduced the hosts to 154 for 9, but could not get the final breakthrough as Shadab and Rauf guided Pakistan to a memorable win in Lahore.
Earlier, Pakistan captain and fast bowler Shaheen Shah Afridi took four wickets to restrict England to 241, despite a fighting century from Ben Duckett.
England, who needed a win to stay in contention for the tri-series after losing their first two matches, struggled to recover after slipping to 19 for 3 on a batting-friendly pitch.
Duckett scored 105 off 111 balls, while Sam Curran made 42 during a 93-run stand for the fifth wicket. Gus Atkinson added an unbeaten 36 towards the end of the innings.
Shaheen finished with figures of 4 for 46, while ODI debutant Razaullah took 2 for 38 as England were bowled out in 46.4 overs.

articles.headline: Don't throw away your old, unsupported Nest gadgets — Do this instead
keyFacts: Google discontinued support for first- and second-generation Nest Learning Thermostats in October 2025.
Users can still adjust basic on-device settings, recycle the devices, or use third-party open-source firmware like No Longer Evil to restore smart features.
Users can take advantage of Google's free recycling program with a prepaid shipping label after performing a factory reset.
body: Don't throw away your old, unsupported Nest gadgets — Do this instead
Google recently dropped support for some of its early smart thermostats.

Google generated a bit of fury in October 2025 when it discontinued support for Nest's first- and second-generation Learning Thermostats. Understandably — while we're all used to upgrading phones and computers on a regular basis, thermostats are relatively permanent fixtures that we depend on for comfort. They're not even that demanding on a software level, so it's not clear why Google couldn't come up with some solution to keep its older models running for more than 14 years.

These products aren't completely useless, to be clear. You can still adjust on-device temperatures and settings, including their auto-schedule functions. But without support on Google's end, they're disconnected from outside apps and accessories, and they're no longer receiving any software updates. The company has tried to make good with discounted upgrades to the fourth-gen Learning Thermostat, but that's obviously not too appealing if you weren't planning to double down on Google's ecosystem.

Thankfully, there are two other options: recycling and switching to a different brand, or turning to third-party projects attempting to resuscitate the old smart features. Which option you go for may depend on your level of tech savvy.
The open-source and recycling options for your Nest Thermostat

The main effort to revive older Nest thermostats is a free, open-source project called No Longer Evil. By flashing your device with custom firmware, you can substitute some or all of the advanced functions that were disabled when Google disconnected you from the cloud. There's actually a No Longer Evil cloud platform, but you can also set up your own server, or connect to the Home Assistant ecosystem.

If any of this sounds intimidating, you might want to stay away. While there's an automated installer that guides you through the process, there's a non-zero risk of bricking your thermostat. If that happens, you won't be able to use it again in any capacity, even its "dumb" form. That could be dangerous if you have to go an extended period without a replacement in hot or freezing conditions.

If the weather is tolerable and you're prepared for an upgrade, it's good to take advantage of Google's free recycling program. You'll get a prepaid shipping label, which saves you the trouble of having to drive anywhere or spend anything. If you don't have access to a printer, however, you'll have to look up what local retailers and e-waste centers offer in your area and do things the hard way. Regardless, be sure to perform a factory reset by going to Settings > Reset > All Settings. You don't want any trace of personal data on something you're handing to a stranger.
Do you really need a new smart thermostat?

It may well be worth investing in a new one from Google or another smart thermostat maker if your goal is to cut energy bills. Better models optimize performance not just in terms of general efficiency, but by detecting occupancy and syncing with cloud-based weather data. If nothing else, it can be helpful to adjust temperatures remotely — when no one's at home, there's no sense wasting money on perfect heating or cooling.

Beyond that, there may not be a real need for you to invest in a new smart thermostat. If the people in your home have predictable habits, you should be fine enough with your Nest's built-in scheduling. Comfortable temperatures don't vary much during the year. If you want to save cash, a simple tactic is to let yourself get a little hotter in the summer, and a little colder in the winter. Changing clothes or using portable fans and heaters is often more economical than forcing your entire HVAC system to work harder.

If you do think it's worth buying a new thermostat, be sure to check for any rebate programs offered by your energy provider. I recently bought a new Ecobee, and the rebate was steep enough that I was able to afford a top-of-the-line model for less than what a midrange one would cost on sale. Entry-level thermostats might as well be free.

articles.headline: Kimi Antonelli storms to US F1 GP victory but is made to wait for title glory
keyFacts: Kimi Antonelli won the US Grand Prix ahead of Charles Leclerc but delayed his Formula One world championship celebration until the next round in Mexico.
Antonelli secured his ninth win of the season from pole position, leading teammate George Russell by 123 points and Lewis Hamilton by 124.
Antonelli needs to finish ninth or better, or ahead of his rivals at the Mexican Grand Prix, to claim the world championship.
body: Kimi Antonelli took a dominant victory at the US Grand Prix, with a controlled and composed drive to beat the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc into second place, but it was not quite enough for the Italian to seal his first Formula One world championship at the Circuit of the Americas. The coronation is surely but delayed for a week as Antonelli has made it almost a formality that he will seal the deal at the next round in Mexico.

Antonelli did everything required of him in Austin, taking pole and converting it to a win, his ninth of the season. With his teammate George Russell finishing in eighth place and Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton in fourth, the fight is alive but only just, and Antonelli is surely now in position to finish the job next weekend in Mexico City.

Antonelli leads Russell by 123 points and Hamilton by 124. With nine wins the Italian cannot be caught on countback and needs only to be 100 ahead after the Mexican GP. Any finish in front of Russell and Hamilton, or ninth or better regardless of where his two rivals finish, will be enough for the 20-year-old to be the youngest driver to claim the sport’s crown and the first Italian to do so since Alberto Ascari won in 1953.

In what was something of a stately affair in Austin, enlivened largely by a split strategy with the Mercedes of Antonelli and Russell opting for a one-stop strategy over the two-stopper of Red Bull and Ferrari, the former proved to be the right call. Antonelli led from the off and after putting in a long first stint while his rivals dashed in for new boots, he emerged able to regain the lead and not have to stop again.

The strategy split made the procession at least open to debate for the mid-period until it became clear that the one-stopper was the quicker option. The late phase did see some feisty passing by Max Verstappen who took advantage of his fresher rubber to hustle through the field, as did Leclerc in his wake who was equally brave and ultimately took second place from the Dutchman who finished in third, albeit with the mitigation of some engine-braking problems. Hamilton too made a late pass to claim fourth for Ferrari with Lando Norris in fifth for McLaren.

The race however belonged to Antonelli. He did not put a foot wrong with a cool-headed display as he assuredly put one hand on the title. The Italian went into the weekend insisting he just wanted to have fun, to perform at his best and not let the title play on his mind. He did so with no little success at the Circuit of the Americas, where certainly he was having a good time.

The pole lap, his first since the Belgian Grand Prix in July, had been brilliant, and in the race he demonstrated the same imperious form as when at his very best this season and which has brought him to within touching distance of his record-breaking achievement.

Just as his five-race run of victories at the start of the season had given him command of the title fight, he is closing it out with nerveless control. The pole, he admitted, had been something of a surprise given how strong Red Bull have been of late but the victory was an emphatic reminder that these are the performances Antonelli is always capable of delivering.

Moreover the result will be welcomed with open arms at Mercedes. The minor wobble they experienced when their upgrades brought to Malaysia did not deliver as expected and left the team having to work at bringing the package up to speed looks to be over.

They have addressed it to the extent that its operating window remains narrower but is more workable, and Antonelli looked to be comfortable in the car which was once more enjoying an advantage over the rest of the field.

It is far from the dominance it enjoyed for the first half of the season but what is of most import for Mercedes is that they appear to have successfully addressed it and have confidence on the direction they are taking with the car next season.

On a circuit which represents an all-round test of a car’s strengths, through high-speed corners, slow-speed sections and demanding, heavy-braking zones, a well-balanced ride is essential and the Mercedes once more looked like it was on rails in Antonelli’s hands.

He went into the race in Austin needing to win and he delivered, with a superb drive indicative of the form he has shown across the season, not quite sufficient to clinch it here, but enough to ensure it is all over bar the shouting.

articles.headline: Trump: Nicki Minaj has ‘one hell of a beautiful a**’
keyFacts: Donald Trump complimented Nicki Minaj's body before she spoke at a Detroit campaign rally on Sunday.
Minaj attended the event to campaign for Republican candidates Mike Rogers and John James ahead of the midterm elections.
Minaj said she has worked with Trump's team and pledged to support him if he runs again.
body: President Donald Trump complimented rap mogul Nicki Minaj’s body before she gave a speech at a campaign rally in Detroit on Sunday.

“By the way, I’ve looked at one hell of a beautiful a** before, Nicki Minaj,” Trump said to roaring applause after similarly praising Sen. Jon Husted’s (R-OH) physique, who Trump campaigned for earlier in the month. “That’s hard to miss. Stand up, that’s hard to miss,” he said as Minaj stood up and waved to the crowd.

Trump’s comment continued his run of mentioning campaign attendees’ bodies in moments that often draw laughter from crowds as he looks to shore up voter support ahead of November’s midterm elections . Minaj was in Detroit to campaign for Republican Michigan Senate nominee Mike Rogers and gubernatorial candidate John James.
Minaj eventually took the stage herself at the tail end of the rally, putting her emcee skills to good use and hyping up the crowd.

The Queen of Rap, as the president referred to her, led the crowd in call-and-response chants boosting both Rogers and James before detailing how she’s worked with the president’s team over the past year.
NICKI MINAJ TEASED AS NEW WHITE HOUSE PRESS SECRETARY

“We really need all of these great people to be elected because this is a major turning point for our country. And when you’re in major states like Michigan, we need this to be a leader in the movement that’s happening right now,” she declared. “So, President Trump, it is an honor to stand with you every single time, and I will continue to support you forever and ever. If you run again, I will support you again.”

“Look at it! Look at this! I mean, everybody, isn’t she great?” Trump added after Minaj left the stage. “She never looked more beautiful, and you see why everybody likes Nicki. Love, like, but she is a very, very special person. She gets it.”

articles.headline: Brazil elections: Vote counting resumes after extension
keyFacts: Brazil began counting presidential election ballots after the Supreme Court extended voting by two hours following campaign complaints.
Left-wing incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva faces right-wing challenger Flavio Bolsonaro in a tight runoff election.
Brazil's electoral court chief said he expects an official winner to be announced within hours of polls closing.
body: What you need to know
- Votes being counted in Brazil's presidential election after polling was extended for 2 more hours
- Lula has won almost 80% of the votes cast by Brazilian voters in Germany
- Brazilians voted in the final round of the presidential election
- Left-wing incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva is facing off against Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of the far-right former President Jair Bolsonaro
- Polls showed the two as neck-and-neck after Bolsonaro beat Lula by 2.2 million votes in the first round
- The 33 million voters who didn't vote in the first round could decide the result if they can be mobilized
Keep reading for the latest updates from the second round of Brazil's presidential election on Sunday, October 25:
Tired of missing our real-time updates? Click here to add us as a Preferred Source on Google. Then tap the "Star" or "Preferred" to keep DW News at the top of your feed.
Votes being tallied in Brazil's presidential election after polls close
The electronic voting system used in the country means that a final result could be determined within a matter of hours, although that final result is expected to be tight.
Here's a DW infographic on where the results stand:
Voting extended after complaints by both sides
Brazil's Supreme Court has moved to extend voting time in the presidential election until 7 p.m. local time (2200 GMT), giving voters an additional two hours.
The decision comes amid complaints from Lula's team that public bus services had been hampered, blocking people from getting to polling stations.
At the same time, Bolsonaro's team complained of weather conditions in certain regions making it more difficult for people to get out and vote.
Lula asks for polls to stay open longer after people 'barred from voting'
President Lula has requested an extension to poll opening hours after buses were taken out of circulation in Sao Paolo, the country's largest city, which he said prevented many people from voting.

"We are asking the Supreme Court to extend the electoral process so that those who were effectively barred from voting, due to the dirty tactics of mayors, can still cast their votes," Lula said, according to AFP.
Lula said 40% of buses in the city had been prevented from going into service, a claim that matched local media reports saying 75 buses had been blocked from leaving garages.
"I've never complained about anything in any election before. Whether I won or lost, I'd just accept it and get ready for the next one. But this time, something abominable is happening," he said.
"No one should give up on voting just because some scoundrel of a business owner or some crooked, criminal mayor tried to stop the people from casting their ballots."
Results show Brazilian voters in Germany back Lula
Brazilians in Germany have voted overwhelmingly for Lula, according to figures posted by Brazilian Embassies across the country and seen by DW's Portuguese service.
The left-wing incumbent, Lula, won 79.09% of the ballots cast by the 20,923 voters across Germany. This marks an increase on the 71.9% he won in the first round.
Brazilian voters in Germany could vote at embassies in Berlin, Hamburg, Cologne, Frankfurt and Munich.

The German capital saw the greatest support for Lula, with 88.77% of the votes going his way. Frankfurt was the city with the greatest support for Bolsonaro, but on 29.03% he still trailed his opponent by some margin.

The turnout also increased in the second round in comparison to the first round when it stood at 19,322. However, for both rounds, only around half of the 41,552 eligible voters turned out to vote. Across the world, there are some 918,900 eligible voters for Sunday's election.
IN PHOTOS: Almost 160 million called out to vote
What role is Trump playing in Brazil's election?
Although he hasn't endorsed either candidate, US President Donald Trump is close to the Bolsonaro family.

Not only did the senior Bolsonaro imitate Trump's rhetoric and policies, he also refused to concede defeat after losing to Lula in 2022, leading to his imprisonment for an attempted coup, provoking comparisons with Trump's own defeat to Joe Biden in 2020.
On the other side, Lula has presented himself as a defense against US interference.
The right "wants to govern with the American flag," Lula said after casting his ballot on Sunday.
A Bolsonaro win would mark a further move in Latin America toward pro-US far-right leaders, following in the footsteps of countries such as Colombia, Chile and Peru.
Results expected within hours of polls closing

The president of Brazil's Superior Electoral Court, Kassio Nunes Marques, has said he expects the winner of Sunday's vote to be announced officially between 8.30 p.m. and 9 p.m. (2330 and 0000 GMT), according to A Folha de Sao Paolo.
Brazil uses an electronic voting system meaning that ballots can be tallied quicker than in elections where paper votes are counted by hand.
However, the gap between the winner and loser is expected to be small, with the two running head-to-head in pre-election polls.
Supreme Court president urges candidates to accept result of vote
The head of Brazil's Supreme Federal Court, Edson Fachin, has called for the candidates to respect the result of Sunday's vote.

"It's important to remember that all authority and power comes from the people and, thus, it is fundamental that the choices that derive from the manifestation of popular sovereignty are respected," he said as he left his local polling station, according to A Folha de Sao Paulo.
"Brazil needs peace and calm to, from tomorrow, be able to confront the major challenges in many areas that demand the presence of the state."
Some observers have posited that Flavio Bolsonaro could refuse to accept a Lula victory, like his father before him, with the potential for violence to erupt.
IN DEPTH: What the election could mean for the Amazon
Brazil is heading back to the polls, but the impact could be felt worldwide.
With the Amazon vital to the health of the planet, the election could help shape its future.
Read DW's full story on the planet-sized consequences of Brazil's election.
WATCH: One community's divide over crime and policing

Rio's deadliest police raid left 122 people dead and divided a community. As voters weigh crime against police violence, Brazil's election battle is playing out in the streets of the district of Penha.
Flavio Bolsonaro urges Brazilians to vote 'rain or shine'

Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro has urged voters to turn out "rain or shine" to change the country's direction, accusing President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva of leaving Brazilians fearful.
"Brazil will change. Brazil will win," said the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, arguing that conditions had worsened over the past four years.
The opposition candidate criticized Lula's record on security and the economy, saying voters should not persist with a "mistake."

Bolsonaro cast his ballot at a school in Rio de Janeiro's Vila Isabel neighborhood around 20 minutes after polls opened. Wearing a yellow shirt, he arrived in the rain with his wife, Fernanda, amid heavy security.
Lula accuses Bolsonaro of preferring the US flag

Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva says voters are choosing between a candidate who defends Brazil's flag and one who prefers the US flag, referring to his right-wing challenger Flavio Bolsonaro.
The right "wants to govern with the American flag," the leftist incumbent said after casting his ballot in Sao Bernardo do Campo, near Sao Paulo.
Lula, who is seeking a fourth, nonconsecutive term, also said Brazilians had taken to the streets to defend their gains.
"What I saw in this runoff was not about a political party or a trade union. People took to the streets to defend their gains," he told reporters.
He also warned about political violence, citing a brick thrown at a supporter of his leftist Workers' Party (PT) in Montes Claros. "It shows what is at stake," he said.
Welcome to our coverage
Thank you for joining us today as we bring you the latest from the final round of Brazil's presidential election.
Polls opened at 8 a.m. this morning (1100 GMT) and are set to close at 5 p.m. (2000 GMT), based on time in the capital Brasilia. The first results are expected 30-60 minutes after polls close.

President Lula, 80, is hoping to turn around his defeat in the first round to Flavio Bolsonaro, 45, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro who is currently imprisoned for trying to overturn the previous election.
Flavio has said he would free his father if he wins and give him a role in his cabinet.

articles.headline: Deeply divided Israel braces for pivotal election
keyFacts: Israel will hold a general election on Tuesday, marking the country's first vote since the October 7 attacks.
Polls show Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's governing coalition and Gadi Eisenkot's centrist opposition bloc are almost neck-and-neck.
The vote could end in a deadlock if neither main bloc secures a majority without the support of Arab parties.
body: - Published
After three years of regional war, this is a battle Israel always knew was coming.
The general election on Tuesday hangs over a country that's deeply divided and ready for a fight.

Polls published on Friday put the governing coalition and the main opposition bloc almost neck-and-neck, with half a million first-time voters due to cast their ballot and some 70,000 Israelis reportedly flying in from abroad specifically to vote.
On Saturday night, vast crowds of opposition voters gathered in central Tel Aviv to demand a change of government.
"We're optimistic," 21-year-old Omri told me. "I want peace, I want security, and I want to end corruption and get the religious fanatics out."
This campaign has been energized by new tactics - including AI videos designed to grab the headlines - and also by a new face.
Gadi Eisenkot is, perhaps, not the man you might expect to take on the flashy, aggressive, media-savvy brand of Israel's longest-serving prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu.

Relatively new to politics, with a working-class Moroccan background, Eisenkot is a former military chief of staff who is renowned for his calm manner and low-drama approach. He's been dubbed by some as a "non-politician".
But he and his centrist Yashar party have regularly pipped Netanyahu and his Likud party to the top spot in recent polls, the last of which was published on Friday, in line with Israeli election law.

Israeli politics is the art of coalition-building, rather than the task of any one party winning power, but with the predicted result too close to call, Eisenkot's rising profile has sharpened a race many Israelis already see as existential for the future of their country.
I watched him slip past the cameras at a community centre for Ethiopian Jews in the city of Ramle last week, through a gaggle of security personnel and advisors.
One of those who had come to hear him speak was David, a smartly dressed man in a freshly-pressed shirt and navy jacket, who said he had met Eisenkot before.
"He looks you in the eye, not like a leader looking down at someone," David told me. "And he listens. He's very sympathetic."

Eisenkot's appeal is often put down to his personal manner and profile. A softly-spoken military man whose son was killed during the Gaza War, he has presented himself as coming "from the periphery", not from Israel's wealthy urban elite.
His Moroccan background became election headlines earlier this month when a pro-Netanyahu speaker used a racist slur to refer to Eisenkot during a TV debate, referring to him as a Moroccan "monkey".

"These elections are about many issues," Eisenkot told the crowd gathered at the Ramle community centre. "They are about security, economy, education...but primarily, they are about the identity of the State of Israel, and what kind of Israel we want to see. A Jewish state, a democratic state, a liberal, tolerant, egalitarian state."

This is music to opposition ears, who say Benjamin Netanyahu's government is a threat to Israel's democracy, pointing to his efforts to curb the powers of the judicial system, and his refusal to establish a state commission of inquiry into the 7 October 2023 attacks on the grounds that the country's Supreme Court would be biased against him.

Eisenkot, along with other opposition leaders, has attempted to draw voters away from Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party by promising such a state inquiry, which a recent survey suggests is supported by more than 70% of Jewish Israelis.
He has also vowed to enforce court rulings on drafting ultra-Orthodox Jews into national military service - another measure that is popular with right-wing voters and opposition alike.
Benjamin Netanyahu has hit back with a campaign focused on Israel's security, and a core campaign slogan of "No Surrender".

He has repeatedly cast his rivals as soft on security, playing on the fears of some right-wing voters that Jewish opposition parties might ally with Israel's Arab parties to secure a majority, and suggesting this could compromise national security.
Around one-fifth of Israel's population is Arab - many of whom describe themselves as Palestinian citizens of Israel.
These are the first elections since the 7 October attacks, in which Hamas-led gunmen stormed through Gaza's border fence, killing almost people and taking 251 hostage.
It was Israel's worst security failure, but three years on its prime minister is again running for re-election as the only man who can keep Israel safe.

"If the army had woken him in time, it wouldn't have happened," Shlomi Bashar told me, one of several die-hard Netanyahu fans drinking in a basement cafÃ© in Jerusalem's Mahane Yehuda market. "He does bear a certain responsibility, but after the 7 October, he changed the entire Middle East."
Netanyahu has been hammering home the message that Israel's wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran, in the years after the 7 October attacks, have reduced existential threats to the country.

"We need him to be re-elected so that he can finish this work," said Shlomi. "In my opinion, he is one of the best leaders in the world. Most of the world loves him and respects him, because he is a strong man and his ideas are correct."

The prime minister has traditionally relied on a stable base of right-wing voters, but is projected to see a thinning of support in this election. Some voters may be slipping away to opposition parties like Eisenkot's. Others, including some die-hard Likud voters we spoke to, said the 7 October attacks had pushed them towards parties further on the right.

Lt Col (Res) Eyal Hajbi, head of the regional civil defence unit in the Netanyahu stronghold of Sderot, right on the Gaza border, lost several friends and colleagues in the attacks. He lights candles for them every day in his office, and told me he would be thinking about them when he cast his ballot on Tuesday.
Standing on a ridge overlooking the ruins of northern Gaza, he gestured to the wasteland where Israel's army has completely flattened the neighbourhoods of Beit Lahia and Beit Hanoun.
"As far as I'm concerned, after 7 October, we should wipe them all out," he said. "I've changed my understanding of Gaza. Before, I wouldn't have said we should destroy it."
He told me he and his family had always voted Likud, but that now he was voting for the far-right party of Itamar Ben Gvir, Jewish Power.
"My family has become more extreme than it ever was before," he said. "If once we deliberated over it, today we don't think twice; we vote."
Polls suggest that less than 10% of Israelis are undecided and that very few of those are considering switching between government parties and opposition ones.
Ben Gvir, National Security minister in Netanyahu's coalition, has been reaching out to younger voters through headline-grabbing social media campaigns.
A poll for one of Israel's leading newspapers, Yedioth Ahronoth, published on 9 October, suggested that more than 16% of first-time voters in Israel would choose far-right parties like his.

In Sderot, a group of 18 year olds from a nearby Jewish religious college told me their political views had been affected by the 7 October attacks far more than their parents. All four teenagers were planning to vote for another far-right party, Religious Zionism, led by Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich.

"Today, the whole younger generation understands that peaceful paths will not work," Aviad Elmahach, one of the teenagers, told me. "Older adults, who are set in a fixed mindset, find [it] harder to change, but the youth understand that we need to be here with strength and an iron fist, which is the only way to win."

The lesson of 7 October, he said, was that Israel needed to be as forceful as possible in its relations with the Palestinians, more than 74,000 of whom have been killed by Israel in Gaza since then, according to the Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.

"The youth have a fresh new perspective that has not yet become entrenched in politics, and they understand very well why we're voting for Smotrich - it means holding the land with strength and giving [the Palestinians] nothing through peaceful gestures."
A little further south along the Gaza border are the kibbutzim that were overrun by gunmen during the Hamas attacks. They were renowned for decades as bastions of the Israeli left.
Among them is Nir Oz, where 47 people were killed and 76 taken hostage that day.

Three years on, residents are moving back. Twenty-six-year-old Gal Pauker has opened a Friday wine cafÃ© at the edge of his small vineyard next to the Gaza border - a few wooden tables set out under sheets of beige canvas to shade customers from the strong desert sun. His grandfather Gideon was killed during the 7 October attacks.
I asked Gal, and his mother Galia, whether the those attacks had shifted their political views.
"We need a change - we can't live with this government anymore," Galia said. "And I'm not talking about security, I'm talking first about humanity."
Having voted for centrist parties in the past, Galia says she's decided to vote for Eisenkot this time around, because "he's an ordinary guy and I hope he'll continue the way he's talking".
Her son Gal said he was deciding between Eisenkot and the left-leaning Democrats party of Yair Golan, another former army general.

"I'm not naÃ¯ve. I know there are a lot of more militant voices from young generations," he said. "I don't know if Eisenkot will be better than Golan in terms of security, but I think we have bigger problems: economics, social problems, education, health. We didn't get new neighbours on October 7 - it was a major event, but didn't change how we see ourselves."

Threats to security versus threats to democracy - these are old political tramlines for Israeli voters, deepened by the 7 October attacks, and by four years of the most right-wing government in Israel's history.
But on some of the biggest international concerns, the differences between government and opposition are not as wide as it might seem.
Gadi Eisenkot has pledged to end Hamas rule of Gaza within 18 months, either through a US-led peace plan, or through "military and operational capabilities".

All the main opposition leaders have voiced support for some form of Israeli settlement in the occupied West Bank, which has expanded massively under the current government and is illegal under international law. None have openly committed to the idea of full Palestinian statehood, something Benjamin Netanyahu has vowed to block. Eisenkot has spoken about creating the conditions for "autonomy or state-minus" under ultimate Israeli security control.

Tuesday's vote could well end in deadlock, with neither government nor opposition able to form a majority without the support of Arab parties, which polls project could win enough seats to be kingmakers. All but one of Israel's Jewish opposition parties have so far rejected working with either of the two Arab party blocs.

With Benjamin Netanyahu ramping up warnings of fresh threats from Iran, opposition voices warning of potential disruption to the ballot, and Israeli rights activists warning of a further spike in violence by settlers in the occupied West Bank, political instability at home could leave Israelis facing both a fresh test of their democracy, and fresh security threats.

articles.headline: FBI tip line and veterans crisis site among 350 federal web addresses exposing visitors to network spies, senator warns
keyFacts: Senator Ron Wyden warned that 350 federal web addresses, including the FBI tip portal and VA crisis line, expose visitor hostnames to network eavesdroppers.
Wyden asked CISA and OMB to mandate Encrypted Client Hello on federal websites and make its support mandatory for federal cloud and network contracts.
Wyden requested an unclassified response and action plan from the agencies by November 20, 2026.
body: - Sen. Ron Wyden wants CISA and OMB to require Encrypted Client Hello on federal websites and make it a federal contract condition
- His list of 350 CDN-hosted addresses without ECH includes the FBI tip portal, the VA's crisis line, and hotlines for whistleblowers and civil rights complaints
- ECH hides site names only alongside encrypted DNS, does nothing for server breaches, and is already blocked in Russia, where some listed embassy pages are aimed

US Senator Ron Wyden (D-Ore.) wants the federal government to turn on a privacy feature that major web browsers have supported for three years, warning that hundreds of agency web addresses still broadcast the name of the site each visitor uses to anyone watching the network along the way.

In a letter to CISA acting director Nick Andersen and deputy federal chief information officer Thomas Flagg, Wyden asked the two agencies to require Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) across federal websites and to make ECH support a condition for cloud and network vendors seeking federal contracts.

The letter attaches a list of 350 executive branch web addresses that use content delivery networks (CDNs) but do not use ECH, while requesting an unclassified response and action plan by November 20 2026.
The one thing HTTPS leaves in the open is the gap being addressed here

Almost every federal site now encrypts the pages people read and the forms they submit. Standard HTTPS does not hide the hostname. When a browser opens a secure connection, it announces the site it wants in a field called Server Name Indication, in plain text, before encryption begins.
An internet provider, a hostile Wi-Fi network, or a compromised telecom carrier can therefore log that a connection went to tips.fbi.gov without reading a word of the tip itself.

ECH encrypts that part of the handshake. It works best behind a large CDN, where thousands of unrelated sites share the same front door. Cloudflare's implementation, for example, presents every ECH-protected site to the network under one shared name, so an observer can tell a visitor is reaching a Cloudflare-hosted site, but not which one.

Wyden's letter singles out two services. The Department of Veterans Affairs' online suicide prevention service at veteranscrisisline.net is hosted on Amazon Web Services, which the letter says does not currently support ECH. The FBI's tip portal at tips.fbi.gov runs on Cloudflare, which does, but the bureau has not turned it on yet, as Wyden noted, stating: "For the federal domains using a CDN provider with ECH support, such as Cloudflare, turning on domain protection merely requires a configuration update."

191 of the 350 addresses, or 54.6%, are diplomatic: 174 embassy sites, three consulates, and 14 missions, mostly to international bodies such as NATO and the UN. Another 53 are subdomains of bie.edu, the Bureau of Indian Education's domain, which appear to be individual school sites. A further 12 are test, training, or staging hosts, including several user acceptance testing subdomains for Education Department debt services.

That leaves 94 addresses outside those groups, and the most troubling entries sit there; they include the DHS inspector general's complaint hotline, the Justice Department's civil rights reporting portal, the intelligence community's job application site, a USCIS tip form, the State Department's Rewards for Justice site, an NIH alcohol treatment navigator, a CDC doxy-PEP site, several federal HIV information sites, and ICE's detainee locator.

Cloudflare's documentation says ECH is enabled by default on Free zones, while customers on other plans must switch it on themselves. That fits the spokesperson's finding: a paying government customer has to opt in. For the FBI, the fix really is a setting.

For the VA, it is not. If Amazon's CDN does not offer ECH, the agency would need to change providers or wait. This is where Wyden's second request, making ECH support a condition of federal contracts, gets complicated.

A procurement rule written today would, in practice, favor a very small pool of providers until others catch up. That may be the intent, since it pressures Amazon and its rivals, but it may be as much a market lever as a security fix, at least in the short term.

ECH does have its limitations, however: the protocol's own specification warns that the destination can still leak through plaintext DNS lookups or the server's IP address. Google made the same point when Android 17 added system-wide ECH in August, saying the feature works "in tandem with private DNS to obscure the domain names you visit."

To reiterate, agencies can enable ECH on their side, but they cannot make a veteran on home broadband use encrypted DNS, therefore leaving the door open to exploitation by someone snooping on the network.

A bigger problem is also international coverage. Many of the highlighted URLs are embassies such as ru.usembassy.gov, by.usembassy.gov, cn.usembassy.gov, and ir.usembassy.gov, all of which arguably have users connecting from relatively hostile networks.

Russia has been blocking Cloudflare's ECH since November 2024, with regulator Roskomnadzor declaring at the time that using it violates Russian law. Russian providers block connections that carry both an ECH extension and Cloudflare's shared outer name, which left Cloudflare customers there choosing between disabling ECH and moving to a domestic CDN.

For an embassy page, enabling ECH could mean trading a visible hostname for an unreachable site in the country where the hostname matters most, making it a difficult tradeoff with only one real solution: skipping ECH for now.

None of this is new territory for Wyden. In October 2018, he wrote to DHS's Chris Krebs urging agencies to adopt encrypted DNS and Encrypted SNI, ECH's predecessor, and asking DHS to work with GSA on making ESNI a condition for CDN vendors selling to the government.

He called that "the next logical step" after DHS's 2017 HTTPS directive, BOD 18-01. The 2026 letter cites the same directive and describes its requests as "the next logical steps." His record on these letters is mixed rather than hopeless. A 2018 HTTPS letter to the Pentagon was followed by a Defense Department plan to secure its websites.

The client side is ready: most major browsers have supported ECH since October 2023, per the letter, and Android 17 now applies it system-wide. The FBI fix is cheap and overdue. But ECH narrows what a passive eavesdropper learns rather than making a visit invisible, and whether this request outlasts the last one may depend less on CISA and OMB than on whether Amazon and others join Cloudflare.

articles.headline: Sydney Sweeney's New Netflix Sci-Fi Space Epic Gets First Details
keyFacts: Actor Noah Centineo revealed on a podcast that Netflix's live-action Gundam film is a big action romance space movie set in the Universal Century timeline.
The cast features Sydney Sweeney, Noah Centineo, Jason Isaacs, Michael Mando, and several other actors.
Netflix has not announced a release date for the film, but filming wrapped in July.
body: The live-action Gundam film has been in the works in some form or another since 2018. A director and cast have been announced, including high-profile names like Sydney Sweeney joining the project. Still, hard details on exactly what Netflix's live-action adaptation of the legendary mech anime series will look like have been almost non-existent.
Now one of the movie's stars is pulling back the curtain ever so slightly.

Appearing on the Happy Sad Confused podcast this summer, Gundam and Street Fighter star Noah Centineo revealed the movie is a "big action romance space movie." Centineo continued by describing Gundam as, "a non-Shakespearean Romeo and Juliet in space." That is a bit of a confusing statement, but what I think Centineo means is that the film is about star-crossed lovers on the opposite sides of a generational conflict. That sounds like it could fit perfectly within established Mobile Suit Gundam lore, as the series often focuses on the war between the Earth Federation and the Principality of Zeon in the Universal Century timeline.
An early official synopsis of the film reads:

As shifting allegiances and a growing threat set them on a collision course for one another, they’re pulled into a high-stakes race across the stars that could define the fate of humanity. With awe-inspiring battles, intimate human emotion, and an epic cinematic scale, this is Gundam like it’s been seen before.

Centineo confirmed to Horowitz that the Gundam film will take place in the Universal Century. This timeline is where a number of the most iconic shows and movies in the Gundam franchise have occurred, including the original series that started it all. While we don't know exactly when in the timeline the live-action film will take place, concept art released in 2021 showed the iconic RX-78-2 Gundam suit from the original series. That concept art, however, was shown while Jordan Vogt-Roberts was attached as director. Vogt-Roberts was later replaced with Jim Mickle.

Noah Centineo and Sydney Sweeney won't be the only familiar faces in the movie. They'll be joined by the likes of Jason Isaacs (Star Trek: Discovery) and Michael Mando (Spider-Man: Brand New Day), as well as Jackson White (Tell Me Lies), Shioli Kutsuna (Deadpool & Wolverine), Nonso Anozie (Sweet Tooth), Javon “Wanna” Walton (Under the Bridge), Oleksandr Rudynskyi (The Agency), Ida Brooke (Dune: Part Three), and Gemma Chua-Tran (Heartbreak High).

Netflix has not set a release date for the movie, but filming wrapped in July. Gundam fans have a lot to look forward to right now. In addition to the live-action movie, a new animated series, Mobile Suit Gundam RG XARX-ZERO, is set to be released in 2027. A game set in the same universe as the show, Gundam Rogue Orbit, will also be released next year.

articles.headline: Marine Le Pen vows French ‘renaissance’ as far right eyes seat of power
keyFacts: Marine Le Pen launched her French presidential campaign in Orleans, promising to restore authority and security during ongoing nationwide protests.
Le Pen's National Rally leads current election polls while capitalizing on widespread public discontent with President Emmanuel Macron's security handling.
The party presented Jordan Bardella as Le Pen's prospective head of government while advocating reduced French contributions to the European Union.
body: Orleans, France – Marine Le Pen took to the stage with a clear message: She would lead France’s “renaissance” as the country sank into crisis – and she would do so soon.

The far-right figure’s words were met with cheers from thousands of supporters gathered in Orleans in central France on Sunday, as she launched her presidential campaign against a backdrop of mass demonstrations and widespread social and economic discontent.
“Marine présidente!” the crowd chanted, waving French flags beneath a sea of red and blue lights. Organisers said 8,500 supporters had gathered in a venue transformed into a fort for the event.
Standing tall on stage in a pink blazer, her hair impeccably coiffed, Le Pen spoke with the confidence of a leader who believes the presidency is within reach.
Riding high in the polls, with candidates from the right, left and centre trailing behind her, she presented the election as a historic opportunity to restore France’s past glory.
“This is a story to be written, a destiny to be fulfilled,” she told the crowd, which erupted in cheers.
Her pitch was a promise to restore authority and security in a country she portrayed as having lost control.
“We are going to re-establish the rule of law,” she said, drawing loud applause from supporters wearing “Marine présidente” T-shirts.
Manon Funeau, 21, a business school student, was among the supporters.
“What they propose are values that resonate with me, that vibrate within me,” she said. “Honestly, I feel at home here.”

Le Pen’s speech comes as the country is at a crossroads. France has been shaken by a wave of protests since mid-September, a movement sparked by high school students in a Paris suburb that grew into a nationwide mobilisation tapping into widespread discontent.
Over the past two weekends, largely peaceful protests have been accompanied by episodes of violence on a scale rarely seen in recent years.

On October 17, shops were looted and ransacked, and more than 2,000 people were arrested as hundreds of thousands took to the streets of French cities. A similar dynamic unfolded the following weekend, though on a smaller scale. The protests show little sign of abating, with calls for further demonstrations already circulating.

The unrest has given Le Pen’s National Rally (RN) an opportunity to play one of its favourite cards: presenting itself as the guarantor of law and order. It has fuelled criticism of President Emmanuel Macron over his handling of public security, allowing Le Pen to accuse him of incompetence and the far-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon – a contender in the coming elections – of encouraging the violence.
‘My country is drifting off course’

“I believe that my country is currently drifting off course,” said Nadede, a 56-year-old who began voting for RN in 2024 over what she said was the country’s growing lack of security. She did not spell out any specific event.
“I think that the only person capable of setting it back on the right track is Marine Le Pen – especially since, up until now, everyone else who has run for office has struggled to do so,” she said.

Outside the convention hall, the scale of the security operation offered a glimpse of the tensions surrounding the event. Police checks began at departure stations in Paris and continued on arrival, while officers in full gear moved through train carriages during the journey.
Orleans itself had been brought to a near standstill. All businesses were shut and public transport suspended.

Standing almost alone in the city’s main square was the statue of Joan of Arc, surrounded only by fences. A day earlier, about 3,000 police officers had been deployed to prevent unrest as anti-RN protesters gathered against what they say is a xenophobic and racist party.

Orleans was no casual choice. For a party that has long sought to cast itself as the guardian of French identity and national sovereignty, the city is inseparable from the story of Joan of Arc, the 15th-century heroine who helped lift the English siege of Orléans in 1429 and became a symbol of France’s resistance and liberation.

For decades, the far right has claimed her as an emblem of national pride, invoking the image of a warrior who came to save France from foreign domination. Le Pen herself has drawn parallels between Joan’s mission and her political ambitions.

The crowd at the RN Congress offered a glimpse of how the party has expanded its appeal to a wider section of society: from young people from urban centres to middle-class workers who used to vote for the centrist party.

Only a few years ago, the party was still considered on the fringes of French politics. Its growth has been driven in part by a carefully crafted strategy known as dédiabolisation, or de-demonisation, developed over the past two decades to broaden the party’s base while tempering its rhetoric and distancing it from positions that had made it toxic to many voters.

The party has long been associated with racism, xenophobia and anti-Semitism. Le Pen’s father, Jean-Marie Le Pen, was convicted of hate speech, including for describing Nazi gas chambers as “a detail of history”. He was expelled from the party in 2015.
Far right ‘gaining ground’

Marine Le Pen has sought to broaden RN’s appeal, combining restrictive immigration policies with promises of social protection. The party has gained ground in working-class areas traditionally associated with the left, including former Communist strongholds, by presenting itself as a defender of public services and the purchasing power of everyday people.

While RN has long abandoned some of its most radical proposals, including leaving the Eurozone and pursuing a fully fledged “Frexit”, the election of such a eurosceptic to the helm of the European Union’s second-largest economy would send shockwaves. She has pledged a referendum to challenge the primacy of EU law over migration policy, as well as an annual 11-billion-euro ($12.3bn) reduction in France’s contribution to the bloc.
The party’s membership has nearly tripled, with approximately 112,000 members now paying their dues, up from fewer than 37,000 in 2022.

“The party has been gaining ground at every level: mayors, deputies, senators. Usually, when a movement seems on the rise, people join,” said Baptiste Roger-Lacan, a historian and political analyst with a focus on far-right parties in Europe. “It also shows how it is less and less socially damaging to be a member of the RN.”

But the party’s programme “is still fraught with fiscal absurdity”, Roger-Lacan said. “They still want to implement racist laws, which are bound to provoke widespread anger, and their diplomatic agenda is still pro-Russian and anti-EU – even if they don’t advocate Frexit any more.”

Jordan Bardella, Le Pen’s second-in-command and Le Pen protégé – an impeccably dressed 31-year-old who looks like a cross between the Wolf of Wall Street and Superman’s alter ego, Clark Kent – also spoke at the event.
“No one should be intimidated by their political opinions,” he said, speaking ahead of his mentor.

Some observers say the October 17 protests and their aftermath have proved a gift to RN, allowing the party to not only reinforce its law-and-order message but also to shift attention away from recent difficulties.

In September, investigative outlet Mediapart published allegations that Bardella had expressed anti-Semitic views in private messages dating back to his teenage years. He denied the allegations and announced legal action against the journalists.
The episode posed a challenge for a party that has spent years trying to shed its xenophobic image and recast itself as a supporter of Israel.

Bardella has also reportedly differed with Le Pen over the party’s economic agenda and whether to make her proposed ban on the wearing of the Islamic headscarf in public spaces a central campaign issue.
Yet, at the Congress, those tensions appeared to have been set aside, at least publicly.
“Marine president – a Bardella government” was the slogan, projecting unity as Le Pen launched her presidential bid and Bardella positioned himself as her prospective head of government.

articles.headline: iFixit’s look inside the iPhone Duo may explain those broken screens and hinges
keyFacts: Repair site iFixit gave the iPhone Duo a 5 out of 10 repairability score, making it the highest score given to a foldable device.
iFixit found that a matte nano-texture cover and specially angled subpixels help mask the screen crease on the iPhone Duo.
iFixit suspects that a complex hinge, an accordion cable, and pressure near the battery may explain reports of cracked screens.
body: As is tradition, iFixit has torn open the latest iPhone and laid its parts bare on a table. It found some interesting details about how Apple might be hiding the crease on the Duo’s folding screen and gave it a 5/10 repairability score. That might not seem particularly high, but it’s the best score the site has given to a foldable yet.
iFixit’s look inside the iPhone Duo may explain those broken screens and hinges
The iPhone Duo is the most repairable foldable yet, but that’s not saying much.

The internal screen’s matte nano-texture cover doesn’t just make it more readable in bright sunlight; it also helps mask the crease by scattering reflections. When looking at the display under a microscope, iFixit also found oval-shaped subpixels arranged at various angles, which the site believes are designed to reduce artifacts and further mask the crease down the middle of the display.

The nano-texture outer layer is relatively easy to replace without swapping out the OLED underneath. If you do need to repair the display itself, however, good luck. As is the case with other foldables, it’s an expensive nightmare. Dust did make it into the USB-C port, speaker grills, and the hinge — making it a bit crunchy. But noticeably less of the glow dust found its way inside the phone than the Z Fold8 or Pixel 11 Pro Fold.

As for reports of damaged screens and cracking hinges, iFixit has some theories. The hinge on the iPhone Duo is incredibly complex, and they suspect part of it sometimes isn’t descending properly. There is also an accordion cable that passes over that exact spot, and it’s near the edge of the battery. It’s possible this is concentrating pressure and leading to the “audible crack” reported by some and the broken screens. Apple did not immediately return a request for comment.

articles.headline: Grok releases the first seven minutes of its AI-generated ‘Odyssey’
keyFacts: Grok released a seven-minute video titled Episode 1 of an AI-generated Odyssey series, created with Wonder Studios and director Dev Walker.
Elon Musk previously criticized Christopher Nolans successful practical film version of The Odyssey over its cast diversity.
The reviewer stated that the Grok footage lacks artistry and human interest, feeling airless and devoid of momentum.
body: Three months after Elon Musk declared that Grok would release a full-length, “historically accurate” movie version of “The Odyssey,” Grok has published a whole seven minutes — what the company is now calling “Episode 1 of our Odyssey series.”

Musk had previously lashed out at Christopher Nolan’s version of “The Odyssey” because Nolan cast nonwhite and transgender actors. And Nolan is, in many ways, a perfect foil for Musk — while SpaceX and Tesla CEO hypes up data centers in space and posts an unending stream of AI-generated content, Nolan has described himself as “a techno-skeptic” and said that before AI, he’d never seen a technology “so completely rejected by the public.”

And while Nolan’s version of “The Odyssey” certainly used plenty of visual effects, it’s primarily a feat of practical filmmaking, with a shoot spanning six countries and a cast and crew of thousands. After its release in July, the film became an extraordinary box office success, selling out Imax screenings for months and becoming the likely front-runner at the next Academy Awards.
As for the Grok version of “The Odyssey” (created in collaboration with Wonder Studios and director Dev Walker), well, you can watch for yourself.

I’ll admit it’s not as spectacularly ugly as I’d expected, and certainly more impressive than other videos that Musk has posted recently. If I didn’t know better, there were moments when I might have thought these were real actors sailing across a real sea. And while I can’t speak to Grok’s historical accuracy, it does seem that all the characters come in a Musk-approved skin color, while the narrator uses a British accent that will sound familiar to anyone who’s played a fantasy video game or watched a generic Hollywood epic from the past 25 years.

What the footage really lacks is any sense of artistry, inspiration, or human interest. The backstory — delivered via the aforementioned voiceover — seems to go on forever, finally giving way to one bearded face after another, each shouting stilted lines that make Nolan’s dialogue sound like Shakespeare.

While a few individual shots might provide a reasonable simulacrum of reality, the whole thing feels completely airless, offering viewers no sense of momentum, no reason to care about anyone or anything on-screen. And where I had no trouble paying attention for the nearly three-hour runtime of Nolan’s “Odyssey,” I was listlessly checking how much I had left before the Grok version was even halfway through.
It’s hard to imagine being interested in another seven minutes of this, much less a full movie’s worth.

articles.headline: Following Cancelled Concert, Umamusume Fans Give Knott’s Berry Farm Blacksmith Busiest Day Of His Life
keyFacts: Publisher Cygames cancelled the first official Umamusume concert in America after recent changes to visa applications prevented musicians and voice actors from attending.
Cygames refunded concert tickets and compensated fans for booked airfare and hotel accommodations.

body: This weekend was supposed to be the first official Umamusume concert in America. That was until a week ago, when publisher Cygames suddenly broke the bad news that they were unable to secure the necessary documentation to hold the event. For fans, it was a load of horse apples. But for the Pretty Derby die-hards, it presented an opportunity to form a new posse, organizing a day out to Knottâs Berry Farmâs ye olde west town and giving their blacksmith the best day of his life.
“I was told that the horseshoe blacksmith at knottâs today had the most business he ever had,” posted one Umamusume in attendance, “his queue for the day completely filled.”

With less than a week from the starting line, Cygames said that Trump’s recent changes to visa applications barred their musicians and voice actors, forcing them to cancel the lone American stop on the world tour. The mobile game, which has since spurred numerous animated series and comics, follows anthropomorphized girls based on real-world racetrack legends. You mix horse people with anime people and you end up with a pretty devout following. But even in lesser circumstances, such a sudden change of plans would feel pretty raw. Thankfully the publisher lessened the blow by compensating for any booked airfare and hotel accommodations, on top of refunding concert tickets.

For those who cleared their schedule anyway, fans in the area decided not to let the bad news break their stride. A herd of Umamusume heads decided to mosey on down to Knottâs Berry Farm. Not for their annual Halloween houses or the Elvira show, but for their ghost town. As in, old-timey cowpoke ghost town. Making a day on the range, showing off plush toys. For horse girls and cow boys alike.

— trustworthy timmy (@nekolelouch) October 24, 2026

It seems that the real star of this community event was Knottâs in-house blacksmith. A tradition since the park opened in 1947, and an institution in the ghost town pavilion, Knottâs keeps the smithy around to forge iron and talk a bit about frontier history. The fixture allows parents to turn their day of thrill rides into a field trip for 20, breath catching minutes.

Every dog has its day. And this metal worker wasnât about to look a gift horse in the mouth. Umamusume booked his day solid, the busiest of his career according to attendees. The fans requested horseshoes branded with the names of their favorite characters who, once again, share their titles with real competing horses. Still doesnât explain why anime girls without hoofs would even need a horseshoe, unless theyâre also susceptible to fungal infections or those gross Facebook reels that keep showing up in your feed.

articles.headline: GOP Mich. Senate hopeful Mike Rogers dodges whether he’s ‘MAGA Republican’
keyFacts: GOP Michigan Senate candidate Mike Rogers deflected questions on whether he is a MAGA Republican during an appearance on Meet the Press.
Rogers is courting Black and Jewish voters by criticizing Democrat Abdul El-Sayed's past ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, which El-Sayed has disavowed.
Rogers and El-Sayed are closely matched in the Senate race, with El-Sayed leading by 1.9 percentage points in recent polling aggregates.
body: “I get you guys on the national press, but this is a little bit disgusting to me,” Rogers said on NBC News’ “Meet the Press” when asked if he’s a MAGA GOPer, while grumbling about the alleged lack of coverage over the defections of supporters that Democrat Abdul El-Sayed has faced.

“The Democrat coalitions that we have are the fastest-growing coalitions we have,” Rogers said. “Jewish Democrats say we can’t vote for [El-Sayed]. African Americans in Detroit and Pontiac and Flint say, ‘We can’t vote him.’ “
Throughout his campaign, Rogers has worked to carefully thread the needle between courting President Trump’s supporters and not scaring off swing voters in Michigan.

To that end, the GOPer has called for an end to the war in Iran while touting his relationship with Trump as an asset that could help him convince the president to wind down the tariffs on Canada that have rocked Michigan.
At the same time, Rogers has worked to capitalize on Democratic unease over El-Sayed, seeking to woo black and Jewish voters to his camp.

“Mike Rogers is also campaigning rigorously in Detroit. I mean, every time you turn around, the guy’s in Detroit,” said Rep. Haley Stevens (D-Mich.), who challenged El-Sayed in the Aug. 4 primary, to CNN on Sunday.
Stevens and other Michigan Democrats have raised alarms about Rogers’ push to win over black voters, historically a core part of the Dem coalition.
Lon Johnson, the chairman of the Michigan Democratic Party from 2013 to 2015, has publicly declared he isn’t voting for El-Sayed.
Of particular concern are ties between members of El-Sayed’s family and the Muslim Brotherhood, which is notorious for radical offshoots that critics claim were the ideological inspiration for Hamas.
In 2012, El-Sayed had been publicly supportive of then-Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi, a leader within the Muslim Brotherhood, and urged him to “purge” the media and police.
“Meet the Press” anchor Kristen Welker pressed Rogers on whether that line of attack might alienate moderate Muslims voters.

“Remember, the Muslim Brotherhood is banned in five Muslim countries,” Rogers shot back. “This is not about Islam. It’s not about how he prays. It is about his adherence to this radical Islamic agenda.

“A lot of the Muslims here are part of our community and an important part of our fabric here,” he stressed. “And what happens with that is they understand that they don’t want to bring that hate, that division.”
El-Sayed has publicly disavowed the Brotherhood.
After his final debate against Rogers last week, El-Sayed accused him of harping on his faith.
“We had a little debate. Or I had a debate, and he just pointed at me and said, ‘He’s Muslim,’ ” El-Sayed grumbled after their verbal bout.
Rogers and El-Sayed are neck and neck in the critical Senate race, with the latter notching a 1.9 percentage point edge in the latest RealClearPolitics aggregate of polls.

articles.headline: Commander Shepard actors Jennifer Hale & Mark Meer mourn BioWare: 'It was in the hands of ownership that may not have understood what BioWare fully is''
keyFacts: Mass Effect voice actors Jennifer Hale and Mark Meer mourned BioWare and expressed concern for newly unemployed employees during an Instagram Live stream.
Hale stated that BioWare was in the hands of ownership that may not have fully understood the company and expressed hope for the franchise's future.
Meer called the closure a massive loss for the video game industry and fans, while confirming that they will still celebrate N7 Day.
body: As reported by IGN, veteran actors Jennifer Hale and Mark Meer, who voiced the female and male Commanders Shepard in Mass Effect, respectively, directly addressed fans of the series in an October 21 Instagram Live. The two reflected on BioWare, and commiserated over its tragic fate. Here are some highlights from each I pulled from the stream:

"I feel weirdly hopeful, and I can’t explain why. I feel for the employees who are suddenly unemployed. That is the number one thing on my mind. Those beautiful team members who are looking for a new home.

"One of the things that has my heart kind of hopeful is that, when I heard about the sale of [EA] some time ago to [The Saudi Public Investment Fund and Jared Kushner], I don't know that they are fans of these IPs, and if they get the gold that they have in their hands.

"It’s really hard to think about BioWare being shut down, but it was in the hands of ownership that may not have understood what BioWare fully is. And I’m hopeful that maybe, there might be some crazy thing where they decide that. in order to increase their profit margins—which is often their priority—they will release these IPs into the market to sell them, and use that to do what they do, which is increase their profit margins. But maybe, someone could grab hold of these IPs and do something with them.
"I don't know if that's possible, but that's where my heart sits. You never know. Heck, let's do a community-based Kickstarter—raise the money, take it over, and do it ourselves. Anything's possible.

"It's wild to watch the consolidation of the industry. Companies are consuming companies are consuming companies. Now they're just these big blobs, and the blobs are beginning to implode. It's not necessarily driven by a creative motive. They're driven by a profit motive. That's their motive, they get to have that.

"But when that cell implodes on itself, all those parts of the cell go out into the world, and they get to reseed somewhere. I just don't feel like it's done. That version of it is done, but the original version of it was done some time ago."

"It is very sad news … It is a massive loss for Edmonton, for Canada, and for the video game industry in general. It’s very unfortunate to see. And of course, I feel very bad as well for all of the fans.
"BioWare was an Edmonton company. It meant a lot to the acting community in Edmonton. There was this major videogame company that was producing games right there in the prairies, in our city.

"I've been talking to fans, and some people were quite distraught—understandably. The thing is, Mass Effect is going to be around as long as the fans keep it alive … Speaking for myself, as long as people keep tagging me in their cosplay pics, or sending me fanart, or tagging me in their fanart, I'll continue to [share it].
"We're still going to be celebrating N7 Day this year … We will come together.
"Next year is the 20th anniversary of the release of Mass Effect 1 … We might not have corporate support behind us, but we're going to be celebrating the 20th anniversary next year."

Both actors' reactions strike me as so characteristic of their respective backgrounds: Hale is one of the voices of videogames (not to diminish Meer's own extensive resume). She jumped to BioWare's place in the industry and its current crisis. Meer, a standby of the Edmonton theater and improv scene, fixated on the closure's effects on this city he clearly loves.
Both are 100% correct about the collective joy and meaning people found in BioWare's work. That's something private equity can't take from us—at least not with current technology.

As for Hale's optimism regarding the rights and potential future of the franchise, well, I Want To Believe. Not to obnoxiously needle what seemed like an offhand idea, but I don't think Kickstarter's walking through that door. Aside from Double Fine's Broken Age and the utterly baffling case of Star Citizen, many gaming crowdfunding successes—like Pillars of Eternity and Wasteland 2—still required further, traditional investment to go gold. BioWare and/or its IP would be orders of magnitude more expensive.

There's also precedent to look back on: EA has not done anything with Ultima in over 20 years. Many people don't realize this series was foundational to the development of both Japanese and Western-style RPGs, as EA's poor stewardship has allowed it to almost completely fade from our collective memory.

But I think we're all still waiting on a hero, a man on horseback, and the only riders with deep enough pockets to intervene here are billionaires, other companies on the scale of EA, or the state. With other publicly-traded companies, you'd risk replicating what BioWare went through under EA. I would love it if the Canadian government stepped in, nationalized BioWare, what have you, but it feels like a pipe dream.

The only semi-plausible happy ending I can picture looks like what happened to The Onion: A benevolent/eccentric super-rich guy steps in to save the day with little concern for profitability. Does anyone know one who enjoys RPGs (or immersive sims, for that matter)?

articles.headline: Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola delays campaign stops after car crash
keyFacts: Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola and her family suffered minor injuries in a car crash on Saturday, her campaign said.
Peltola is challenging Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan in a high-stakes race for Alaska's lone seat in the US Senate.
Peltola rescheduled multiple campaign stops to recover, with plans to resume touring on Tuesday in Homer, her campaign said.
body: Mary Peltola, a Democrat who is running for Alaska’s lone US Senate seat, and her family suffered minor injuries in a car crash while driving to a campaign stop on Saturday, her campaign said.

The family was on its way to the Alaska Federation of Natives annual banquet when another vehicle crashed into the one transporting Peltola and her family, her campaign said in a statement on Sunday. Peltola required medical attention after the collision.

“Mary and her family sustained minor injuries but are in good spirits,” Cheryl Bruce, Peltola’s campaign manager, said in a statement. “Unfortunately, per the advice of medical professionals, Mary’s upcoming events in Fairbanks and Bethel will be rescheduled for later in the week as she takes time to recover.”

Bruce added: “Mary is disappointed that the accident is delaying the start of her Alaska Always tour, and she is eager to get back on the campaign trail to speak directly with Alaskans about her plan to take on the rigged system and lower costs for working families.”

Police responded to a “multi-vehicle collision” at about 6.55pm on Saturday, according to the Anchorage police department. Peltola’s family and the occupant of a second vehicle were taken to a local hospital “with non-life-threatening injuries”, according to the authorities, while the occupant of a third vehicle refused medical transport.
“The circumstances of the collision are under investigation,” reads a statement from the police department.

Peltola, an Alaska Native and former congresswoman, is challenging Republican incumbent senator Dan Sullivan, hoping to become the first Democrat in nearly two decades to represent the state in the Senate. Both candidates have tried to rally support from Alaska Native voters, a key constituency in the high-stakes race that has become one of the most watched in the nation.

On Friday, Donald Trump ordered the justice department to block the certification of the Senate election in Alaska if Sullivan loses. The lawsuit cites potential confusion with another Republican candidate who is listed on the ranked-choice ballot as Daniel J Sullivan Jr, who is a retired schoolteacher.

Peltola’s incident delayed what her campaign announced as the “Alaska Always tour,” an eight-stop push through the last week before election day. Her campaign said she will resume events on Tuesday, with a stop in Homer, Alaska.

articles.headline: Ousting Hegseth ‘priority No. 1’ if Democrats retake majority, Rep. Jason Crow says
