body: Rep. Jason Crow (D-CO) said Sunday that ousting War Secretary Pete Hegseth is his “priority No. 1” if the Democrats retake the House of Representatives in November’s midterm elections.

A member of the House Armed Services Committee, Crow was asked by Margaret Brennan on Face the Nation about reports that Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton “received intelligence that Iran has substantially increased efforts to target U.S. personnel” in the Middle East.
“We know that the U.S. has drawn down from some military bases, some diplomatic posts,” she said. “What, if anything, can you tell us about this plot?”

“Iran remains a danger,” Crow said before attacking the administration’s handling of the Russia-Ukraine war and the conflict in Iran . “Pete Hegseth remains incompetent and is not doing what’s necessary to protect our service members, which is why he’s my priority No. 1 if we retake the majority, to make sure we oust him from the Pentagon, because our service members actually deserve competent, serious, real leadership that will protect them and do the right thing.”

Democrats are broadly expected to investigate members of the Trump administration and potentially attempt to impeach President Donald Trump himself if they retake the House. Brennan mentioned CBS News’s most recent polling, which shows “Democrats are on pace to have a narrow majority of about 11 seats.” She also asked Crow about a recent controversy involving Sen. Elissa Slotkin (D-MI), who faces Senate ethics complaints that argue she deterred young professionals from serving in the Trump administration after making comments at a university event.
HEGSETH’S ‘ARSENAL OF FREEDOM’ TOUR AND ‘SEND ME’ TOURS RESEMBLE A CAMPAIGN TRAIL

“The key here is we don’t want people to want to go work for a corrupt administration to try to line their pockets, like that is not servant leadership,” Crow answered. “If the message being sent from Donald Trump is, hey, come work for me and you’ll get a lot out of it, and you’ll get rich doing it. That’s not actually public servants.” Trump told the Washington Examiner he is “allowed” to preemptively pardon junior staffers after being asked about a report on Saturday that said, “White House attorneys are evaluating whether to issue mass pardons to junior staffers.”

Democrats and Republicans sharpened their attacks on each other over the weekend. Former President Barack Obama went after Trump at campaign stops in Ohio and Michigan on Saturday, while Trump spoke in Georgia on Saturday and Michigan on Sunday.

articles.headline: Clayface Looks Like a Win for the DCU After Earning $43 Million in Box Office Opening Weekend
keyFacts: The DCU film Clayface earned an estimated 43 million dollars globally during its opening weekend.
The R-rated horror film earned 24 million domestically and 19 million internationally, nearly matching its reported 44 million budget.
DC Studios co-chairman James Gunn stated on Threads that he is really proud of the film's A- CinemaScore.
body: Clayface looks set up to be a win for the DCU after securing the top spot at the box office with an estimated global haul of $43 million.

It's a strong start for the low-budget DCU film, split between $24 million domestically and $19 million internationally. The opening weekend total falls toward the higher end of early projections as audiences showed up to see Tom Rhys Harries bring a twisted and often overlooked Batman villain to the big screen.

With brutal body horror elements in a story that sees the birth of its titular character, Clayface follows Matt Hagen as he attempts to rebuild his life after a horrible attack leaves his face scarred. Starring Harries, directed by James Watkins, and written by Mike Flanagan and Hossein Amini, this latest DCU movie took viewers into the darkest corners of James Gunn and Peter Safran's universe they've seen yet, with a pretty hard-R rating.

It's for these reasons that the DCU's foray into a new live-action Gotham City left fans with question marks as they feared how a more adult-oriented story could fit into the same world as something as bubbly and bright as 2025's Superman. So far, at least, it seems to have paid off, at least compared to Supergirl , which landed as a dud in the DCU earlier this year.

The Milly Alcock-led superhero movie was deemed a box office bomb after it premiered in June. That's mostly due to its almost $200 million budget, which towered over the comparatively measly $126.46 million it gathered throughout its run (via Box Office Mojo ). Clayface, on the other hand, is starting its time in theaters almost matching the $44 million budget reported by Variety .

Although there is certainly plenty of ground to cover before officially being declared a success, it seems like a strong start. A few factors will help carry Clayface throughout the rest of its run: Firstly, its October release timing means Halloween moviegoers will have something spooky to watch next weekend. Reviews have been pretty solid, too, with Rotten Tomatoes recording a 75% from critics and 94% from audiences.

Gunn, at least, is proud of Matt Hagen's live-action introduction in the DCU. As viewers went to theaters to squirm at Clayface's backstory, movie fan surveyor site CinemaScore polled an "A-" from audiences. It's a feat rarely seen in the horror genre, something the DC Studios co-chairman made sure to note in a post on Threads .

"Really proud of this," Gunn said. "Sinners is the only horror movie to have EVER gotten an A CinemaScore, and only three horror movies have gotten an A- in the last couple years – Obsession, Weapons, and, now, Clayface. As always, all praise goes to James, Mike, Hossein, Tom, Naomi and the whole gang."

Clayface is in good company in the horror world and in its opening weekend. Coming in second, domestically, was Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim's Elizabeth Holmes documentary, You Can See Everything . After a limited launch drew rave reviews and positive earnings last weekend, the three-hour movie returned for its second bout with an additional $19.5 million. That's a 25% increase from its debut, driven by wider availability across an additional 1,800 theaters in the market.

Strong word-of-mouth could see the Fielder picture continue to attract viewers in the coming weeks as moviegoers dare to dip their toes into Holmes' world and the story of Theranos. Stop-motion studio Laika, meanwhile, might be in for a rough time. Its latest claymation feature, a fantasy epic directed by Travis Knight called Wildwood , came in third at the domestic box office with $11.77 million. That's above projections for the Coraline moviemaker but still far, far below its reported budget of $100 million.

Though still well above 2019's Missing Link, Wildwood's opening weekend numbers put it toward the lower end of debuts in the studio's history, too. Those who have seen Laika's latest might be surprised to hear it could struggle to recoup costs, as Laika has managed to pull some remarkably strong reviews so far. Rotten Tomatoes shows it with a 100% from critics and 97% from audiences. We here at IGN gave it an 8/10 , calling it an "arresting, exciting fantasy epic made all the more impressive by the fact that it's handmade and hand-animated."

Other box office highlights as we approach Halloween are Street Fighter , which brought another $16.8 million worldwide in its second weekend. Alexander Skarsgård and Olivia Colman's Wicker had a domestic total of $5.75 million in its more limited first weekend.

For more on the biggest movies of the weekend, you can read IGN's 7/10 Clayface review . You can also read why we thought You Can See Everything is a 10/10 . articles.headline: 187K+ fans call for EA to "Save Mass Effect"
keyFacts: A petition demanding continued development for the Mass Effect franchise has surpassed 187,000 signatures following BioWare's closure.
Petition organizer Joe Smith called on EA to properly fund the franchise or license the intellectual property to another studio.
The petition follows recent widespread job cuts by EA that also affected developers at Respawn, Maxis, and other studios.
body: A petition created to save BioWare's well-loved sci-fi RPG, Mass Effect, has topped 187,000 signatures.

We said a sad farewell to BioWare earlier this week. Job cuts, coming just months after Saudi Arabia's $55bn leveraged buyout of the company, were anticipated by experts, but drew widespread condemnation and messages of sympathy from across the industry.

Joe Smith, credited with starting the petition, isn't necessarily asking EA to change its mind about BioWare; instead, the petition calls for "decisive action by committing to the continued development of Mass Effect".
"This commitment requires proper funding, adequate staffing, and time allocation to maintain and advance the high standards the franchise is known for," the Change.Org page reads.
"Alternatively, EA could consider licensing the Mass Effect intellectual property (IP) to another studio that shares the passion and vision to keep it alive and allow it to flourish anew."

The petition adds: "Fans around the globe have invested thousands of hours exploring the galaxy, forming deep connections with its multifaceted characters and compelling storylines. It is a franchise that has transcended the typical gamer experience, creating a community that advocates for choice, individuality, and shared adventure. The potential cessation of new developments in this universe is a devastating prospect not only for fans but for the diversity of narrative-driven games as a whole."
Yesterday, we reported that a content creator claiming to have served on a BioWare community council shared alleged details about the cancelled next Mass Effect game, titled Mass Effect Universe.

In a lengthy Twitter/X post, the YouTuber claimed he'd had access through his role on the "Mass Effect Council", had seen firsthand what BioWare was developing, and had provided feedback during development.
This follows the appearance of an internal trailer for Mass Effect Universe, which BioWare later confirmed was real after the company’s closure and the game's cancellation.
EA's widespread job cuts also hit developers at Respawn, Maxis, Full Circle, EA Motive, and other EA-owned studios.

articles.headline: Putting Control Resonant Under A Microscope Is Rewarding In An Unexpected Way
keyFacts: GameSpot reported that Control Resonant shifts its setting from the mystical Oldest House to the borough of Manhattan.
Remedy concept artist Mikko Kinnunen said the game avoids generative AI, using human-authored art and developer likenesses for signs.
The article states that Manhattan's diverse billboards and posters use purposeful contrast and mundane details to give the city a unique history.
body: Over many years, I've written tens of thousands of words covering the Remedy Connected Universe, the Finnish studio's world tying the Alan Wake and Control series together. This is a team that loves rewarding players who notice the smaller details and go off the golden path in search of morsels of understanding. Connecting dots is often much of the fun in a Remedy game.

To my surprise, that side of the developer wasn't on display much in Control Resonant. There are definitely a few nods, and one chain of side quests in particular seems to have greater implications for the studio's future connected-universe games, but overall, I was taken aback by how disinterested Resonant was in tying itself to Remedy's bigger picture. However, it was by looking for those hidden details that I discovered something else I ended up loving about the sequel in a different way.

Even before I played Control Resonant, I was up to my old habits of streaming its trailers in 4K, freeze-framing, rewinding, and dissecting every scrap of detail I could pull out. What's its significance? Where have I seen this name before? What might this logo reference? Time after time, I couldn't find anything relevant to the lingering plot threads we were left with from 2024's Alan Wake 2 and 2019's Control.

In retrospect, it makes perfect sense. Control takes place in the Oldest House, a bureaucratic yet mystical space that is one part House of Representatives, and one part House of Leaves. The place was understandably littered with clues about the grander story being told in Remedyland.

But Control Resonant breaks down those walls and sets protagonist Dylan Faden out into the borough of Manhattan. Sure, like the Oldest House, the city is under siege from its own paranatural threats, but prior to that, it was just a city. So why should every inch of it be hiding more details about what Alan Wake or Saga Anderson are up to?

"It was important for us that our version of Manhattan has a character of its own," Remedy concept artist Mikko Kinnunen told me. "We were aiming for a timeless feel that plays with archetypal New York elements from movies such as Taxi Driver, avoiding direct comparisons to modern-day reality. [...] It was important for the city to feel like a character that has a life and history of its own, and we did not lean heavily into fourth-wall-breaking elements for this reason."
Remedy said some signs around the city are purposely mundane...

It was only when I stopped searching for things like hints of what Wake's agent, Barry Wheeler, is up to--like Alan Wake 2 provided--that I could appreciate what Resonant's finer details did offer. In place of puzzle pieces, I found a wide-ranging voice in the city's billboards, posters, flyers, and more.

Even better, none of it seemed to be done with generative AI, which Kinnunen confirmed, adding that there's "a feeling of cohesion you get when everything is authored by artists with a shared creative intent. It’s not just what the artwork looks like, but why is it there in the first place?"

Of the 60+ hours I've seen put into Resonant, I've several hours closely examining the city's signage. I've come to appreciate how many of them use photos of the developers, which Kinnunen said were the result of an "internal lighthearted casting round" in which Remedy developers had their likenesses photographed, then used in scenarios that fit their vibe, such as gym staff and restaurant employees.

In another game, signs and billboards using real-life photos of people might be jarring, but Remedy has been mixing media forms as long as it's been around, so I didn't think anything of it other than, "who are these people?" and "it's so cool that they did all this instead of taking an AI shortcut." Similarly, he told me the animals featured on the game's signs are the companion animals of Remedy's staff, as you might have guessed.
...while others are there for a specific purpose.

I noted the wide-ranging styles of the various billboards. Resonant's version of Manhattan wisely does not maintain one consistent voice. Instead, some posters are funny-looking, like an enraged man who was "fired over nothing" advertising a law firm, or a plethora of signs that cleverly use the word "control" as a minor wink at the player.

It reminded me of when the studio disguised the @ControlRemedy Twitter account as a brand of medicine until it was ready to flip the switch and announce the game at E3 2018. Remedy has always loved using names for irony, juxtaposition, or signs of nominative determinism. Just ask Max Payne.

Speaking of juxtaposition, I also love how the Federal Bureau of Control's messaging changes slightly when the shadowy organization finds itself public-facing. Kinnunen explained the intention behind that.

"If you look closely, the FBC has a different tone of voice towards the public than what they do internally. The internal, retro-style posters from the first game have made a return, yet we also have expanded upon them. Some PSAs aimed towards the civilians try to play it straight, yet the FBC still manages to make them creepy and funny by being slightly out of touch with modernity."
Does anyone else love fake movie posters in media? I sure do.

In every corner of the virtual city, I found intentionality, even as the point was sometimes merely to be plain, as was the case with the names of some businesses, the artist revealed. I could've saved a lot of time early on had I stopped trying to connect non-existent dots between Armistone building company and the Blessed Organization, a mysterious group in Control lore that I was sure would turn up more in Resonant--until it didn't.

"We wanted to mix a grounded feel of authentic-sounding names with more bespoke, authored ones. For example, [the in-game art studio] 'Könstig' has a few meanings in the Swedish language. Konst means art, and Konstig means strange (among other translations). 'Taikoo House' [sushi bar] is a favorite of mine," he teased, noting that he didn't want to spoil why.

Mirroring my colleague Tauriq Moosa's recent feature on the theme of contrast in Control Resonant , Kinnunen told me how many of the signs players see around the city have a purposeful counterpiece somewhere else, such as the politics-tinged billboards that, in one case, boast that there's "nothing more American" than oil with one that, in another case, demand climate action.

"There are multiple themes going on in various Zones that feature similar contrasts as these 'satirical jabs' mentioned. The key is to evoke a feeling or atmosphere without pushing any specific agenda. Growth versus sustainability is just one of many topics in the advertisements," he said, adding that "the themes are there to complement the setting of each Zone. The wealthy financial district of the Evacuation Zone feels different from the more blue-collar Central, for example. Everything is there to make the world feel a certain way, rather than trying to tell the audience what to think."
The billboards urging climate action purposely play off of the others that celebrate America's dependence on oil.

From theater marquees and coffeehouse chalkboards to sales flyers and calls for political action, the game is loaded with easily missed details, clever nods, and thematic relevance. It's all there, inviting players to inspect it, only with far different results than I assumed when I first began studying Resonant's trailers like the Zapruder Film months ago.

Remedy games have trained me to take a closer look for 16 years now, so my methodology didn't change when I first jumped into Control Resonant. But as clues to my favorite puzzlebox all but dried up completely, the purposeful, human-made details that were there instead became symbols of a new appreciation for one of video games' most creative studios.

articles.headline: 'Grossly Incompetent': Trump Loses It Over Obama, El-Sayed In Early Morning Meltdown
keyFacts: President Donald Trump criticized former President Barack Obama on social media after Obama campaigned for Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed.
Trump insulted Obama's presidency and launched attacks against El-Sayed, while endorsing Republican candidate Mike Rogers.
Obama had previously criticized Trump during a Michigan rally and addressed attacks on El-Sayed's background.
body: President Donald Trump flipped out on his predecessor Barack Obama early Sunday morning after he attacked his administration while campaigning for Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee for a U.S. Senate seat in Michigan.
“Obama was a grossly incompetent President!” began Trump in a 12:42 a.m. post to his Truth Social platform.

“He paid off Iran with $Billions, and gave them a road to a Nuclear Weapon. He said that Crooked Hillary Clinton was going to WIN, he campaigned hard for her, and she lost in all directions and ways. He then campaigned full out for Kamala, and likewise, she lost.”

Trump proceeded to turn to Islamophobic attacks to refer to El-Sayed, writing, “Now he’s campaigning for a Muslim Brotherhood Jihadist, who hates Jews and Blacks and AMERICANS and TRUMP, and he is going to lose, also. He’s a Fake Doctor, who runs what is considered to be the WORST CLINIC IN AMERICA.”

“I won Michigan, BIG, have brought back the Car Industry, the Air Force Base, and everything else. Also, more jobs than ever before. Michigan doesn’t want an arrogant, Open Borders, Fake Doctor, Jihadist, whose reputation will only get worse as more information is revealed - And there’s plenty. VOTE FOR MIKE ROGERS! He will never let you down! President DONALD J. TRUMP.”

The post arrived just hours after Obama — in one of his first rallies for this year’s midterms in Michigan, one he also used to back Michigan gubernatorial nominee Jocelyn Benson (D) — slammed Trump’s “corruption,” “cruelty and chaos” and called out the “foolishness” of his administration.

Elsewhere, he appeared to tie attacks hurled at El-Sayed — whose Muslim identity and background has been a focus of his GOP opponent Mike Rogers — to those he faced from Trump through his racist “birther” conspiracy theories.

“Whenever a movement builds to challenge that broken system, the people who benefit from the status quo will say and do anything to stop that train from coming,” he said. “They will use lies and they will use fear and they will use division. And they may even use your name to suggest that you are dangerous and less than trustworthy and less patriotic and less American than they are.”

He emphasized, “We have seen this movie before. I starred in it. I’ve got a long form birth certificate to prove it. This stuff didn’t work on me, not in Michigan. It’s not going to work on Abdul. He is as Michigan as it gets. Abdul was born here. He was raised here.”

articles.headline: Is the Ninja MultiPot the Kitchen Appliance You Need, or Just the One You Want?
keyFacts: Ninja recently released the 12-in-1 MultiPot XL, a $250 countertop appliance featuring a 7.5-quart Megazone or two smaller 3.5-quart pots.
Testing showed the MultiPot XL excels at searing, sautéing, and boiling, but its slow cooker function produced less impressive results than a traditional Crockpot.
The reviewer stated the MultiPot XL is a good option for those with limited space who want a versatile appliance, though not a strict necessity.
body: When I think of kitchen brands dominating home kitchens and wishlists alike, Ninja immediately comes to mind.

Beyond the company’s viral social media videos and massively popular product releases, like the Crispi air fryer and Creami frozen dessert maker, the brand’s popularity may also be rooted in its rapid product launches. Ninja releases products fast, and it releases a lot of them.

In the last couple of months alone, we’ve seen the release of the Prepi, CrushBoss, NeverQuit cookware and now, the MultiPot XL. With colder weather setting in, the 12-in-1 cooker caught my eye. Theoretically, it can reduce kitchen clutter by replacing numerous other countertop appliances, but is it truly a worthy replacement for your Instant Pot, Crockpot and even the classic Dutch oven?

With so many new releases, how do you separate want from need? We cooked numerous meals with the new MultiPot XL to see whether the shiny new appliance has what it takes to earn a place on your countertop.
Searing, sautéing and soups
The Ninja MultiPot XL has 12 functions and the option to cook in the “Megazone,” a 7.5-quart pot, or in two smaller pots, each 3.5 quarts. All of the pots are ceramic-coated.
The first meal I cooked in it was homemade ramen, and I learned there are a few settings where the MultiPot excels, including the sear/sauté function.

The first ingredient I sautéed was mushrooms with butter. The MultiPot quickly preheated and sauteed the mushrooms just as well as a non-stick pan on a stovetop would. When the lids are shut, the pot quickly gathers steam to help speed up the cooking process too.

Next, I placed the chicken thighs in the already heated pot, and they took only a few minutes to cook all the way through. The best part was that the chicken developed a crust, which added extra flavor to the dish.
I used the same function for a handful of additional ingredients, combined everything in the pot with chicken broth and then set the MultiPot to its hot pot setting until everything came to a boil.

Because the pot was already hot, it didn’t take long to boil. When I was ready for it to stop, I turned off the appliance and lifted the pot off the hot plates so it wouldn’t overcook. Over the next couple of weeks, I continued to use the appliance for various meals, but sauté/sear and hot pot remained among my favorite functions.
It’s not a slow cooker replacement

Despite its ability to sear and sauté just as well as a non-stick pan on the stovetop, one setting was less impressive. I used the slow cooker setting to cook a small batch of beef short ribs in one half of the cooker, cooking them on low for over 8 hours. I’ve cooked this meal before in a slow cooker, and by the end of the 8 hours, the meat is usually falling apart and my whole house smells like the dish.

With the MultiPot, though, although the meat was still fully cooked through and had a great flavor, it wasn’t fall-off-the-bone cooked. I’m not entirely sure why that is, but it made me wish I’d cooked that dish in my Crockpot instead.
On the other side of the MultiPot, I cooked brown rice, and it cooked just as well as on the stovetop.

In my experience, the only place where the MultiPot has a leg up on a slow cooker is the fact that you can sauté or sear directly in the MultiPot, then turn the pot to the slow cooker setting, instead of having to sear in a separate pan on the stovetop, then transfer the ingredients to a slow cooker. So, if you’re looking for convenience, the MultiPot offers it.
Who’s the Ninja MultiPot XL best for?

If you have limited countertop space for appliances and want just one that can handle many cooking tasks, the MultiPot XL would be a great option. With 12 settings, it has more versatility than many competitors, but keep in mind that the “keep warm” function is included in the 12, and some functions won’t be used as much as others, such as sous vide.

At $250, it’s more expensive than standard slow cookers and Instant Pots, but it could be a good option if you often cook large meals for a group. If you’re looking for a cheaper multicooker, but want to stay in the Ninja family, the 8-in-1 Ninja PossibleCooker may be a smarter buy since it’s less than half the price but still has the essential functions. However, I haven’t tested the PossibleCooker myself.
The MultiPot XL can definitely be a great choice for some, but I wouldn’t put it in the must-have category, even if the rose quartz option is one of the cutest appliance color schemes I’ve seen.

articles.headline: Want to build a UK datacenter? Please hold while Whitehall transfers you
keyFacts: Building a UK datacenter involves navigating three government departments covering datacenter policy, telecoms, and energy.
Junior minister Liz Lloyd told MPs that datacenter policy falls under BIST while digital infrastructure sits within DCMS.
Microsoft recently withdrew plans for a major AI supercomputer due to challenges in securing power for the facility.
body: Building a UK datacenter spans three government departments: one handles datacenter policy, another telecoms, and a third energy.
MPs this week explored what Prime Minister Andy Burnham's summer reshuffle means for businesses navigating Whitehall.

Liz Lloyd, parliamentary under-secretary of state, sits across two departments with a portfolio of responsibilities as long as a weekly shopping list. She explained to MPs this week that, following the decision to get rid of the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT), liaison with the tech industry on datacenter construction fell to the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST).
Lloyd, who works across BIST and the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS), went on to explain that digital infrastructure sits within DCMS.
Speaking to the House of Commons Science and Technology Committee, Lloyd acknowledged that some departmental responsibilities overlapped.

"In terms of sector responsibilities, that is clear that technology, sorry, that telecom sits with DCMS and datacenters with BIST. When you're actually in an industry or you're trying to run a business, that that that is clear," the junior minister said.

Any business trying to build a datacenter might also want to know how to get power to it. As far as The Register can figure out, that would be the Department for Energy and Net Zero. Planning permission rests with local government, although the overall policy lies with the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government. It may be clear, but it is hardly simple.
The problem is real, though. Earlier this month, Microsoft pulled out of plans for Britain's largest AI supercomputer because of difficulties securing power for the facility.
Elsewhere in the hearing, Lloyd was asked about the government's early 2025 claim that modernizing aging technology and digitizing processes could deliver £45 billion in productivity savings.

Asked if the government stood by the figure, the junior minister said: "The £45 billion figure was an estimate of long-term productivity gains. It wasn't a kind of one-off figure for savings… it was never a figure that was a target or a cashable savings figure."

When the figure was publicized under the Starmer government in January 2025, the press release was headed "Archaic tech sees public sector miss £45 billion annual savings." It continued: "Taxpayer funded services from the NHS to local councils are missing out on £45 billion in productivity savings because they are too often dependent on old and outdated technology."
It claimed the government would "tackle these issues" using "digital tools, AI and common sense to overhaul public sector technology." ®

articles.headline: A 1,000-mile cloud on Mars may reveal physics never seen in nature
keyFacts: A 1,000-mile cloud forms and disappears near the Martian volcano Arsia Mons every morning during spring and summer.
Scientists recently modeled the cloud's formation for the first time using computer simulations.
Study lead author Jorge Hernández-Bernal said the results suggest the cloud is driven by theoretical physics never before observed in nature.
body: Every morning during the Martian spring and summer, a thin and extremely long cloud emerges, only to disappear again. The wispy formation appears near the volcano Arsia Mons and gradually elongates until it reaches over 1,000 miles—about the distance from New York to Kansas City as the crow flies—before dissipating. This cycle then repeats for several months.

Since it was first recorded by a probe in 2018, scientists have been unable to find a plausible explanation for the existence of this cloud, often referred to as the Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud (AMEC). Until now. Recently, researchers successfully modeled the cloud’s formation for the first time, their results suggesting that it may be driven by a physical process that has never been directly observed in any planet's atmosphere.

"We found that we needed to include some exotic physics… physics that, while included in textbooks, is treated as theoretical and usually thought not to happen in nature. It certainly hasn’t been seen in action before," Jorge Hernández-Bernal, a planetary scientist at Paris’ Sorbonne Université and lead author of the study, said in a press release . "Once we included this physics in our simulations, the AMEC emerged just as we hoped.”

articles.headline: UK to invest £100m in 'world first' AI Biosecurity Lab
keyFacts: The UK government announced a 100 million pound investment in a national AI Biosecurity Lab to strengthen defences against biological threats.
AI Minister Kanishka Narayan stated the new lab will bring together scientific expertise to safeguard citizens from emerging risks.
OpenAI and Anthropic will support the lab by providing 200 million pounds worth of AI model credits.
body: - Published
The UK says it will establish a national AI Biosecurity Lab (AIBL) to help strengthen its defences against emerging biological threats.
As part of Wednesday's Budget, the government will commit Â£100m to establishing the new, "world first" institute with the support of leading AI firms.
The chancellor will also pledge millions of pounds in spending across a range of initiatives aimed at shoring up the UK's ability to respond to evolving cyber, biological and AI-enabled threats.
"AI will transform daily life: every firm, community, hospital, school, and every aspect of our economy can benefit," John Healey said.
"I understand and share the concerns of working people, so I am setting out a distinctively British approach to AI.
"One that doesn't leave workers behind and defends our national interest, while ensuring the benefits of AI-enabled growth are felt right across the country."
The full details about the role and remit of the new lab are yet to emerge.

But the AI Minister Kanishka Narayan said it would be a "major new global institution" that brings together "world-leading scientific expertise" to ensure the UK can safeguard its citizens and goals as AI develops.
"That means staying ahead of emerging threats, from cyber attacks to biological risks, while building more of the critical technology our security depends on," he said.
"By backing British science, advanced chips and our own AI companies, we can strengthen our national security, rebuild Britain's industrial strength and create good, skilled jobs across the country."
The AI Biosecurity Lab's creation will also be supported by leading AI developers, with OpenAI and Anthropic providing Â£200m worth of AI model credits that can be spent on the use of their models.
The Chancellor's plans to boost AI spending will also see an additional Â£120m committed to the UK's AI Security Institute (AISI).

Established by the former Conservative government in 2023, the lab evaluates the risks of the most advanced and powerful models - and has been championed for its role in helping build a collaborative and open approach to AI testing.

The additional funding announced by the Chancellor will aim to help ensure the lab can continue its efforts and work, particularly amid growing calls for technical standards and guardrails for AI development.

It will come alongside a Â£60m investment in what it coined a "National Cyber Shield" which it said would use agentic AI to boost cyber-defences, and Â£70m funding towards a National Exposure and Real-Time Vulnerability (NERV) Centre.
This, it said, would harness AI tools to detect cyber vulnerabilities across the UK's critical infrastructure and economy.

It comes after the UK government revealed it was among organisations around the world to have taken some sites offline as a precaution after critical flaws were surfaced in a popular programming language.

Researchers who helped surface the vulnerabilities in PHP - a popular server-side scripting language used in web development for decades - warned platforms which use it could be exposed to potential hacks.
There have been no reports of any successful exploits of the flaw, coined php2shell, so far.
But experts have warned that the incident shows how quickly and easily bugs which have lain long dormant may be surfaced - and potentially exploited - using AI.
